title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 67
paragraphs: That is how the deposing of Demaratus from the kingship came about. As for his flight as an exile from Sparta to the Medes, it happened on account of an insult, as I shall now relate. After he had been stripped of the crown, Demaratus was serving in a public office to which he had been elected. It was the time of the festival of the Gymnopaediae, and Demaratus was among the spectators. Leotychides, who had now become king in his place, sent his servant to ask Demaratus mockingly and insultingly what sort of thing it was to hold a magistracy after having been king. Stung by the question, Demaratus replied that he himself had now had experience of both, whereas Leotychides had not — and that this question would prove the beginning of either endless misfortune or endless good fortune for the Lacedaemonians. With these words he veiled his head, left the theater, and went home. There he at once made ready and sacrificed an ox to Zeus, and after the sacrifice he summoned his mother.
